prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2005 manifesto sets out a progressive, forward-not-back programme: government’s duty is to secure opportunity and security for all, rejecting false choices between wealth creation and social justice, liberty and safety, or national interest and global responsibility.

Record and foundations
- Eight years of stability and growth, low inflation and interest rates, highest employment on record, two million fewer in poverty.
- Major reinvestment and reform in public services: more teachers, nurses and police; faster NHS treatment; crime down 30%; strong schools results.

Opportunity economy
- Keep low debt, independent Bank of England and 2% inflation target; no rise in basic/top income tax rates; targeted family support.
- Full-employment ambition (80% employment), welfare-to-work with obligations and help; reform Incapacity Benefit via Pathways to Work.
- Back enterprise, manufacturing and science (R&D to 2.5% of GDP), proportionate regulation, competitive energy mix including renewables, nuclear and clean coal.
- £180bn+ transport investment to 2015; consider road pricing; rail upgrades, Crossrail, high-speed options.
- Fairness at work: stronger minimum wage, modern trade-union partnership, equalities agenda; CAP and rural reform.

Education: personal to each child
- Personalised learning, strong discipline, parents as partners; all secondary schools specialist, expanding Academies (200 by 2010) with fair admissions.
- Raise quality and status of vocational routes: 14–19 specialised diplomas, more apprenticeships; no drop-out at 16.
- HE expansion with fair funding: fees capped at £3,000, more grants and bursaries; 50% participation aim; stronger science base.

Safe communities
- Neighbourhood policing teams nationwide; tougher action on antisocial behaviour and alcohol-fuelled disorder.
- Cut crime by tackling causes: drugs testing and treatment; Serious Organised Crime Agency; tougher weapons laws; reduce reoffending; stronger victims’ rights.

Fair, firm migration and secure borders
- Points-based system prioritising skills; English tests for settlement; penalties for illegal working; faster decisions.
- Stronger borders with biometrics and ID cards to tackle abuse, illegal work and identity theft; fair, efficient asylum.

NHS: free to all, personal to each
- No charges for operations; cut waits to 18 weeks referral-to-treatment by 2008; real patient choice; expand capacity including community hospitals and independent/voluntary providers at NHS standards.
- Tackle MRSA; integrate health and social care; strong public health drive on food, activity and smoking; improve school meals; dentistry review.

Older people and families
- Pensioner poverty cut via Pension Credit (uprated with earnings); towards long-term pension settlement by consensus; flexible work and individual care budgets.
- End child poverty in a generation; universal Sure Start Children’s Centres; affordable childcare 3–14; longer paid maternity leave (towards 12 months), more flexible working; expand homeownership and quality social housing.

Britain strong in the world
- Lead in a reformed EU (referendum on Constitutional Treaty); NATO at core; support democracy in Iraq; Middle East peace.
- Climate leadership: meet Kyoto, cut CO2 by 20% by 2010 and 60% by 2050; drive renewables and efficiency.
- Africa and development: double aid, debt relief, IFF; universal access to AIDS treatment; fair trade and Doha; end privatisation conditionality.

Quality of life and culture
- Free national museums; broaden participation through Creative Sparks; community sport for all; 2012 Olympics legacy; modern libraries; digital switchover; strong, independent BBC.

Devolution and democratic renewal
- More neighbourhood power, stronger local government, council tax discipline; deepen devolution in nations and regions; complete Lords reform; strengthen equality and human rights with a Single Equality Act.
